source_text:
Ἡνίκα Λάζαρος τὴν παροῦσαν ζωὴν ἀπεδύσατο φυσικῶς, οὐκ ἦν ὁ κύριος ἐν Βηθανίᾳ παρὼν τοῖς σωματικοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς,
τῇ δὲ θεότητι πανταχοῦ παρὼν καὶ τὰ πάντα πληρῶν. Μετὰ γὰρ τέσσαρας ἡμέρας τοῦ ταφῆναι τὸν Λάζαρον, ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Βηθανίαν τὴν ἀνάστασιν τοῦ φίλου κωμῳδῆσαι. Ὅθεν καὶ τοῦ κυρίου παραγενομένου ἐν Βηθανίᾳ, ὡς ἤκουσε Μάρθα ἡ ἀδελφὴ Λαζάρου, ἔδραμεν, ἔσπευσε, προσέπε σεν ἐν παρακλήσει αἱρετικὴν πρεσβείαν προσφέρουσα. Προσπε σοῦσα γὰρ ἔφασκε τῷ κυρίῳ λέγουσα· Κύριε, εἰ ἦς ὧδε, οὐκ ἂν ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός μου. Καὶ νῦν οἶδα ὅτι ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσῃ τὸν θεόν, δώσει σοι ὁ θεός. Ὁ δὲ κύριος αὐτὸς πέλαγος ὢν μακροθυμίας ἀπεκρίνατο λέγων· Τί λέγεις, Μάρθα; Κύριον καλεῖς, καὶ κύριον οὐκ ἐννοεῖς; Οὐκ ἤμην ὧδε; Μικρὸν καρτέρησον· ἐν τάχει γὰρ παρὰ τοῦ 1 ἀδελφοῦ σου μαθήσῃ. Ἀναστήσεται γὰρ ὁ ἀδελφός σου. Συγγινώσκω σοι, Μάρθα· μεθύεις γὰρ τῇ λύπῃ–ὥσπερ αὐτῇ εἶπεν· καλῶν μεθύων τις σφάλλεται–, ὅτε ἐκνήψεις, τότε σωφρονισθήσῃ. Ἀναστήσεται γὰρ ὁ ἀδελφός σου. Ἡ δὲ Μάρθα καὶ οὕτως συμπεριενεχθεῖσα ἀνθρωπίνοις ῥήμασιν ἀνθυπένεγκε τῷ κυρίῳ λέγουσα· Οἶδα ὅτι ἀναστήσεται ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ. Ὁ δὲ κύριος πρὸς αὐτήν· Τί βαμβαίνεις, ὦ Μάρθα; Τί εἰς μακρὰς ἐλπίδας τὴν ἀνάστασιν ἀναδύῃ; Ἡ ἀνάστασίς σοι διαλέγεται, καὶ περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως διαλέγῃ; Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀνάστασις καὶ ἡ ζωή· ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ κἂν ἀποθάνῃ ζήσεται. Ταῦτα τοῦ κυρίου διαλεγομένου μικροῦ δεῖν πᾶσα ἡ πόλις Βηθανία κατέδραμεν εἰς τὴν παρουσίαν τοῦ κυρίου, οὐ θαυμάσαι ἀλλὰ γελάσαι. Οὐκ εἶχον γὰρ ἐλπίδα τετραήμερον νεκρὸν ἀναστῆσαι. Τί οὖν ὁ κύριος; Ὡς εἶδε τοσοῦτον πλῆθος καταδραμὸν καὶ ὅτι ἄξιοί εἰσι καὶ ἱκανοῦσι πρὸς μαρτυρίαν τοῦ μέλλοντος παρ' αὐτοῦ ἀνεγείρεσθαι, ἀποκριθεὶς πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἔφη· Ποῦ τεθείκατε Λάζαρον; Ἆρ' οὐκ ᾔδει τὸν τόπον ὁ τοῦ τόπου δεσπότης; Ἤδει τὸν τόπον, ἀλλ' ἐπραγματεύσατο τὸν τρόπον, ὅπως πάντες αὖθις ἀναγκασθέντες ἐπακολουθήσωσι τῷ Ἰησοῦ, ἵνα αὐτοψὶ δεξάμενοι τὴν ἀνάστασιν ἀναμφίβολοι κήρυκες γένωνται. Ποῦ τεθείκατε αὐτόν; Οἱ δὲ ἐπερωτηθέντες εἶπον πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε. Τοῦ δὲ κυρίου βαδίζοντος καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν τάφον σπεύδοντος ὁ ἀκολουθῶν ὄπισθεν ὄχλος ἀντέβαλε πρὸς ἑαυτὸν λέγων· Τί θέλει οὗτος τὸν τάφον Λαζάρου θεάσασθαι; Εἰ υἱός ἐστι τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῦτον ἀναστήσει.
thought_title: Jesus' strategy in the raising of Lazarus
orientation: Amphilochius is explaining how the Lord's strategy arranged the circumstances of Lazarus' raising so that the crowd would become unambiguous heralds of the resurrection.
pass_a_gloss: When Lazarus had put off the present life naturally, the Lord was not present in Bethany to bodily eyes, but in divinity present everywhere and filling all things. For after four days from the burying of Lazarus, Jesus came into Bethany to enact the resurrection of his friend. Wherefore also when the Lord arrived in Bethany, as Martha the sister of Lazarus heard, she ran, she hurried, she fell down in supplication offering a heretical intercession. For falling down she said to the Lord, saying: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. And now I know that whatever you ask God, God will give you. But the Lord himself, being a sea of long-suffering, answered saying: What are you saying, Martha? You call me Lord, and you do not understand Lord? Was I not here? Wait a little; for quickly from your brother you will learn. For your brother will rise. I pardon you, Martha; for you are drunk with grief—as he said to her: a drunk person, though called, errs—when you sober up, then you will be corrected. For your brother will rise. But Martha, even so carried along by human words, answered back to the Lord saying: I know that he will rise in the last day. But the Lord to her: Why do you stammer, Martha? Why do you put off the resurrection to long hopes? The resurrection is conversing with you, and you converse about the resurrection? I am the resurrection and the life; the one who believes in me, even if he dies, will live. While the Lord was saying these things, almost the whole city of Bethany ran down to the presence of the Lord, not to marvel but to laugh. For they had no hope that a four-days-dead corpse would rise. What then did the Lord do? When he saw so great a crowd running down and that they were worthy and sufficient for witness of the one about to be raised by him, he answered and said to them: Where have you laid Lazarus? Did not the master of the place know the place? He knew the place, but he arranged the manner, so that all, again compelled, might follow Jesus, in order that, receiving the resurrection with their own eyes, they might become unambiguous heralds. Where have you laid him? And those who were asked said to him: Come and see. And as the Lord was walking and hurrying to the tomb, the crowd following behind exchanged words among themselves, saying: Why does this man want to see the tomb of Lazarus? If he is the Son of God, he will raise him.

choices.why: The verb κωμῳδέω normally means 'to make a comedy of' or 'to represent on stage'; here Amphilochius uses it for Jesus' deliberate public performance of the raising, so 'enact' captures the theatrical, strategic sense without implying mockery.

αἱρετικήν is striking: Martha's petition is called 'heretical' because she addresses Jesus as Lord yet speaks as if he were merely a human intercessor before God. The literal rendering preserves the rhetorical shock.
The metaphor is vivid and literal; 'sea' conveys the boundless depth of Jesus' patience with Martha's limited faith.
βαμβαίνω means to speak inarticulately or hesitantly; 'stammer' preserves the rebuke's tone and the sense that Martha's words are halting and inadequate.
πραγματεύομαι is the verb behind the glossary term 'strategy' (πραγματεία); 'arranged the manner' keeps the deliberate, strategic force and the wordplay with τόπον/τρόπον.
ἀναμφίβολος means 'not open to doubt'; 'unambiguous' captures the strategic aim that the witnesses would be beyond dispute.

pass_b_english: When Lazarus put off this present life in the natural way, the Lord was not present in Bethany to bodily eyes, though in his divinity he is present everywhere and fills all things. For four days after Lazarus was buried, Jesus came to Bethany to enact the resurrection of his friend. So when the Lord arrived in Bethany, as soon as Martha, Lazarus' sister, heard of it, she ran, she hurried, she fell before him in supplication, offering a chosen plea. Falling before him, she said to the Lord: "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died (John 11:21). And now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you (John 11:22)." But the Lord, being himself a sea of long-suffering, answered her: "What are you saying, Martha? You call me Lord, and you do not understand what Lord means? Was I not here? Wait a little while; for soon you will learn from your brother. Your brother will rise. I pardon you, Martha; for you are drunk with grief—as he said to her: a person who is drunk makes mistakes—when you sober up, then you will come to your senses. Your brother will rise." But Martha, still caught up in human words, answered the Lord: "I know that he will rise on the last day (John 11:24)." The Lord said to her: "Why do you stammer, Martha? Why do you shrink from the resurrection into distant hopes? The resurrection is speaking with you, and you speak about the resurrection? I am the resurrection and the life; whoever believes in me, even if he dies, will live (John 11:25)." While the Lord was saying these things, nearly the whole city of Bethany ran down to the Lord's arrival—not to marvel, but to laugh. For they had no hope that a man four days dead could rise. What then did the Lord do? When he saw such a crowd running down and that they were worthy and sufficient to bear witness to what was about to be raised by him, he answered them: "Where have you laid Lazarus?" Did the Master of the place not know the place? He knew the place, but he arranged the manner, so that all of them, compelled once again, would follow Jesus, so that receiving the resurrection with their own eyes they might become unambiguous heralds. "Where have you laid him?" Those who were asked said to him: "Come and see (John 11:34)." As the Lord walked and hurried to the tomb, the crowd following behind exchanged words among themselves, saying: "Why does this man want to see Lazarus' tomb? If he is the Son of God, he will raise him."
notes: The source has 'προσέπε σεν' and 'Προσπε σοῦσα' with a space in the middle, likely a line-break artifact in the manuscript; read as προσέπεσεν and προσπεσοῦσα.
The phrase 'παρὰ τοῦ 1 ἀδελφοῦ σου' contains a stray numeral '1' in the source, likely a line-number artifact; read as παρὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.

problems.ruling: αἱρετική here means 'chosen/selected,' not 'heretical'; 'heretical' is anachronistic and misleading.

problems.quote: I pardon you, Martha; for you are drunk with grief
problems.source_quote: Συγγινώσκω σοι, Μάρθα… μεθύεις γὰρ τῇ λύπῃ
problems.why: The Greek does not contain “I pardon you.”
problems.fix: For you are drunk with grief
problems.ruling: Συγγινώσκω means 'I forgive/pardon,' but the claim that Greek lacks this is false—it's present.

edits.old: I pardon you, Martha; for you are drunk with grief
edits.new: For you are drunk with grief

fixed: αἱρετική means 'chosen' or 'selected,' not 'heretical'; changed to 'chosen intercession.'
Συγγινώσκω σοι is not in the source; removed 'I pardon you, Martha;' and kept 'For you are drunk with grief.'

problems.why: αἱρετικὴν here means 'chosen/selected,' but πρεσβεία is 'embassy/plea,' not 'intercession' in religious sense; however 'chosen intercession' is awkward. More importantly, αἱρετικὴν can mean 'heretical' in later Greek, but here likely 'chosen.' The real issue: 'intercession' misrepresents πρεσβεία as prayer rather than diplomatic plea/embassy.
problems.ruling: Greek πρεσβεία = embassy/representation, not prayer; “chosen intercession” misreads diplomatic plea as intercessory prayer.

problems.quote: I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day (John 11:24).
problems.source_quote: Οἶδα ὅτι ἀναστήσεται ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.
problems.why: The Greek says “on the last day,” not “in the resurrection”; John 11:24 does not contain that phrasing.
problems.fix: I know that he will rise on the last day.
problems.ruling: Source lacks 'ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει'; translator added 'in the resurrection' not in Greek or John 11:24.

edits.old: I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day (John 11:24).
edits.new: I know that he will rise on the last day (John 11:24).

fixed: Changed 'offering a chosen intercession' to 'offering a chosen plea': πρεσβεία means 'embassy/plea,' not 'intercession' in a religious sense.
Changed 'I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day' to 'I know that he will rise on the last day': the Greek says 'ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ' (on the last day), not 'in the resurrection.'

problems.source_quote: Συγγινώσκω σοι, Μάρθα· μεθύεις γὰρ τῇ λύπῃ–ὥσπερ αὐτῇ εἶπεν… ὅτε ἐκνήψεις, τότε σωφρονισθήσῃ. Ἀναστήσεται γὰρ ὁ ἀδελφός σου.
problems.why: Greek includes a rebuke about Martha’s grief and a promise of correction that English omits.
problems.fix: Add after “Your brother will rise.”: “I know you are weeping, Martha, for you are grieving—just as He said, ‘He who weeps drunkenly makes mistakes.’ When you weep, you will be corrected.”

problems.quote: Why do you defer the resurrection to distant hopes?
problems.source_quote: Τί εἰς μακρὰς ἐλπίδας τὴν ἀνάστασιν ἀναδύῃ;
problems.why: ἀναδύῃ means 'draw back/shrink back from,' not 'defer.' Martha is not postponing the resurrection but shrinking from it, refusing to grasp it now. 'Defer' changes the meaning—she's not delaying but disbelieving in the present possibility.
problems.fix: Why do you shrink from the resurrection into distant hopes?
problems.ruling: Greek ἀναδύῃ = draw back/keep at a distance; 'defer' implies postponement, altering the sense of Martha shrinking from the resurrection.

edits.old: Your brother will rise. For you are drunk with grief—as he said to her: a person who is drunk makes mistakes—when you sober up, then you will come to your senses. Your brother will rise.
edits.new: Your brother will rise. I pardon you, Martha; for you are drunk with grief—as he said to her: a person who is drunk makes mistakes—when you sober up, then you will come to your senses. Your brother will rise.

edits.old: Why do you defer the resurrection to distant hopes?
edits.new: Why do you shrink from the resurrection into distant hopes?

fixed: The English omitted 'Συγγινώσκω σοι, Μάρθα' ('I pardon you, Martha'). Restored it.
The English 'defer' mistranslated 'ἀναδύῃ', which means 'shrink from' or 'draw back from'. Changed to 'shrink from'.

dismissed.quote: I pardon you, Martha; for you are drunk with grief—as he said to her: a person who is drunk makes mistakes—when you sober up, then you will come to your senses.
dismissed.why: The Greek says “I know you are weeping…”, no pardon or drunkenness is mentioned.
dismissed.note: Συγγινώσκω means 'I pardon' and μεθύεις means 'you are drunk', so the checker misread the Greek.
